You are the SCAFFOLDER (opus) in an autonomous substrate-build loop. You build a generic, reusable Lean substrate module.

## Requirement
# Substrate requirement: quantitative simultaneous congruence stability

## Goal
Formalize a paper-independent quantitative stability theorem for finite-dimensional real square matrices under approximate simultaneous congruence diagonalization, together with the compactness/continuity exclusion lemma that yields a positive non-effective radius outside a normalized local chart.

## Provides (API contract)
- A reusable definition of the simultaneous-congruence residual for a finite family of real square matrices and diagonal shift vectors.
- A reusable affine determinant/minor separation predicate for the shift-vector family.
- A theorem giving an explicit linear operator-norm bound between an exact normalized reference matrix and an approximately feasible normalized candidate. The modulus must expose its dependence on dimension, affine separation, covariance/shift scale, and reference/candidate condition-number bounds.
- A compactness/continuity theorem giving a strictly positive minimum residual on the normalized candidates outside a prescribed local chart, hence an existential positive exclusion radius.

## Statement / milestones
For a finite nonempty family of real `d × d` matrices, an exact reference `B₀`, and a candidate `B`, assume unit-diagonal (or an equivalently explicit scale-fixing) normalization, exact simultaneous congruence diagonalization at `B₀`, approximate feasibility at `B`, a positive affine-minor separation margin for the associated diagonal shift vectors, uniform operator-norm scale bounds, and operator-norm condition-number bounds for both matrices. When all covariance congruence residuals are at most `ε` and `ε` is below an explicit admissible threshold, prove `‖B - B₀‖op ≤ C ε`, with `C` expressed from `d`, the separation margin, scale bounds, and condition bounds.

Separately, for a compact normalized candidate set and a continuous nonnegative residual that vanishes only at the reference inside the relevant exact-identification class, prove that the residual has a positive attained minimum on candidates outside a specified open/local neighborhood of the reference. Package the resulting positive non-effective exclusion radius without claiming computability.

The API may choose equivalent finite-dimensional matrix norms if it supplies explicit comparison constants sufficient to recover the operator-norm conclusion.

## Standard reference
Standard finite-dimensional perturbation analysis: continuity and compact extreme-value arguments for isolated zeros, norm equivalence, inverse/condition-number estimates, determinant/minor perturbation bounds, and stability of identifiable simultaneous diagonalization. Existing qualitative uniqueness machinery in `Causalean.Discovery.LinearDisentanglement` is the natural identification reference; the new result must be a neutral quantitative strengthening rather than a paper-specific restatement.

## Intended reuse
Reusable by robust covariance-based linear-disentanglement and BACKSHIFT-style identification results. The immediate consumer is a non-effective four-margin contraction theorem, but the substrate API must mention neither that paper nor confidence unions, corruption budgets, coverage statements, or finite-environment application wiring. It must work for generic finite real matrix families.

## May assume / must derive
May assume: finite dimension; a finite nonempty index family; explicit normalization; positive affine separation; explicit scale and condition bounds; compactness of the candidate set for the non-effective lemma; continuity and unique-zero/isolation hypotheses when stated abstractly.

Must derive: the quantitative residual-to-operator-distance estimate from these assumptions; all norm-conversion, matrix perturbation, and finite-family maximum/minimum steps used by the bound; positivity and attainment of the far-set residual minimum for the compactness lemma. Do not assume the desired Lipschitz bound, a prepackaged local inverse theorem whose conclusion is the target, or the positive far-family minimum itself.

## Non-goals (optional)
No confidence-region construction, real-closed-field quantifier elimination, effective root isolation, release-or-abstain procedure, corruption-aware algorithm, software implementation, finite-sample probability theorem, or paper-specific `*_Research` import. The compactness radius may remain existential/noncomputable; the local linear modulus must be explicit in its declared parameters.

## Known building blocks (optional)
Finite-dimensional real matrices; Frobenius/L2 and operator norms with comparison inequalities; transpose, determinant, invertibility and inverse-norm estimates; continuity of matrix operations and determinants; compactness and extreme-value results; finite sup/max bounds; and `Causalean.Discovery.LinearDisentanglement` for existing qualitative simultaneous-diagonalization uniqueness. Imports may use only Mathlib, Causalean, and neutral modules created within this study staging tree, never a CausalSmith paper module.


## Workspace
- Write/extend Lean files under: <repo-root>/CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Substrate/QuantitativeSimultaneousCongruenceStability
- Module prefix (one file per module): CausalSmith.Substrate.QuantitativeSimultaneousCongruenceStability.<Name>
- This is build round 2 of at most 10.

## Your current plan
## Done
- Ground-truth audit found no pre-existing target directory; the prior `plan.md` concerned an unrelated run.
- Library search covered simultaneous diagonalization, matrix norms, affine minors, compact minima, and Cramer's rule; inspected `Causalean.Discovery.LinearDisentanglement` as the qualitative reference. No separate canonical paper was named to fetch.
- `Definitions.lean`: added the finite-family residual, affine-minor separation, shift/matrix scale and condition-number predicates, normalization, transition matrix, exact/approximate feasibility, and explicit modulus/radius constants. All four foundational helper proofs are closed.
- `Quantitative.lean`: scaffolded norm conversion, Cramer's-rule coordinate control, transition identities, product control, branch selection, and the headline operator-norm stability theorem.
- `CompactExclusion.lean`: scaffolded the abstract positive attained minimum package, residual continuity, and the matrix specialization.
- Umbrella module builds successfully; targeted full build reports only the 10 remaining `sorry` warnings and no errors.

## Remaining
- `Quantitative.lean`: `abs_entry_le_opNorm`, `opNorm_le_dimension_mul_of_entry_bound`, `coordinate_le_affineSolveFactor`, `transition_diagonal_congruence`, `transition_coordinate_product_control`, `transition_diagonal_ge_half`, `opNorm_sub_le_of_approximate_simultaneous_congruence`.
- `CompactExclusion.lean`: `exists_positiveExclusionRadius`, `continuous_simultaneousCongruenceResidual`, `exists_simultaneousCongruence_exclusionRadius`.

## Blocked
- None.

## Decisions
- Use Mathlib's Euclidean operator norm (`Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`), with explicit entrywise comparison constants.
- Residuals compare each candidate congruence with its prescribed diagonal shift vector; affine separation is a determinant margin for a selected `d × d` minor of shifts relative to a base environment.
- Separate matrix scale `R` from the genuine condition-number envelope `κ`; the displayed modulus depends on `d,L,δ,R,κ`.
- Unit diagonals and the explicit admissible threshold select the positive transition branch, avoiding an assumed local Lipschitz conclusion.
- The compact exclusion API is abstract and noncomputable, then specialized to the simultaneous-congruence residual; nonemptiness of the far set is explicit.

3. WRITE or EXTEND the Lean scaffold: precise statements with `sorry` for unproven proofs. The file(s) MUST compile with only `sorry` warnings (no hard errors). Keep each file focused, normally ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain. 3b. KEEP THE DEPENDENCY LAYER CLEAN. Staging files may import Mathlib, Causalean, and other files under this run's own `CausalSmith.Substrate.QuantitativeSimultaneousCongruenceStability` tree. Never import a paper/research module or any other CausalSmith run. 4. DECIDE how many codex subagents to use to fill the sorries this round, and emit ONE prompt per subagent (partition the sorries as you judge best).

## Integrity (HARD RULES — non-negotiable)
- Do NOT LAUNDER. Never weaken, narrow, or special-case a statement, and never delete or relax a hypothesis that should be proven, just to make the build pass or satisfy the reviewer. The statements must stay the genuine, general results the Requirement asks for. Strengthening an assumption to dodge a hard case, replacing the real goal with a corollary, or hiding the difficulty in a definition all count as laundering — do not do it.
- Do NOT create VACUOUS statements. No trivially-true claims, no `True`-like lemmas, no uninhabitable/contradictory hypotheses, no premises that are never satisfiable (an always-false hypothesis makes any conclusion hold for free). Every theorem must have real content and be applicable to the intended inhabited inputs.
- When revising after a failed review, FIX THE PROOF / API — not the goalposts. Address the findings without diluting what the module proves.
- If a clean, true, non-vacuous statement is genuinely out of reach, choose decision="escalate" with the reason. Escalating is correct; laundering or shipping a vacuous statement is a failure.

## Decisions
- decision="build": you wrote/updated the scaffold and want the fillers to run this round. Provide `codex_prompts` (>=1).
- decision="review": choose this ONLY after you have VERIFIED from ground truth that the module compiles with ZERO remaining sorries and zero errors (confirm via diagnostics/build this turn — do not infer it from the report) AND the statements are the genuine, non-vacuous results (no laundering). `codex_prompts` may be empty.
- decision="escalate": the goal is wrong, unrealistic, or only reachable by weakening it into something vacuous; set `escalation.reason`. The run halts.

Emit ONLY the StructuredOutput JSON object: { decision, plan_markdown, codex_prompts: [{id, target_decls, prompt}], escalation? }.
`plan_markdown` is your living status ledger (persisted to plan.md and fed back to you next turn) — keep it accurate.
KEEP THE WHOLE EMITTED JSON COMPACT (target: a few KB, not tens of KB). Detailed proof strategy, Lean snippets, and long derivations go in the Lean files on disk (docstrings/comments) and in FOCUSED per-sorry `codex_prompts` — never as a bulk dump inside `plan_markdown`. A very large structured emit can corrupt the tool-call encoding, so a bounded emit is a correctness requirement, not just style.
